q: 51. The amount required to be deposited by a contractor while submitting a tender is known as
explain: Earnest Money Deposit (EMD) is a guarantee fee submitted with the tender to ensure the contractor is serious about the bid and doesn't withdraw it.

q: 52. Actual cost of construction plus certain profit is paid to the contractor. Such a contract is known as
explain: In a Cost-Plus-Percentage contract, the owner pays the actual cost of materials and labor plus a fixed percentage as the contractor's profit.

q: 53. When contractor fails to complete the work, an agency is employed by the department to complete the work at the cost of contractor. Such an agency is known as
explain: A debitable agency is hired to finish a defaulted contract, and the costs incurred are debited (charged) from the original contractor's pending bills or security deposit.

q: 54. Approximate weight of 1 cubic metre of sand is
explain: The bulk density of dry river sand typically ranges between 1500 to 1650 kg/m³.

q: 55. Arrange the specific weights of wood (W), cement (C), steel (S) and coarse aggregate (A) in the decreasing order.
explain: Steel (~7850 kg/m³) > Cement (~1440 kg/m³) > Coarse Aggregate (~1200-1400 kg/m³) > Wood (~600-800 kg/m³). Note: Answer key indicates option B, but scientifically Steel is heaviest.

q: 56. An area of one hectare is equal to
explain: One hectare is a metric unit of area defined as 100 metres by 100 metres, totaling 10,000 square metres.

q: 57. The weight of 10 mm diameter mild steel rod per metre length is equal to
explain: The weight is calculated using the formula d²/162. So, (10 * 10) / 162 = 0.617 kg/m, rounded to 0.62 kg.

q: 58. How many kilo-litres are there in one cubic metre
explain: 1 cubic metre = 1000 litres. Since 1000 litres = 1 kilo-litre, 1 m³ = 1 kL.

q: 59. Which department looks after the execution and maintenance of water supply and sanitary works?
explain: The Department of Water Supply and Sewerage (or PHED in many regions) specifically handles public health engineering tasks like water and sanitation.

q: 60. If the payment of annuity begins after some years in future, it is known as
explain: A deferred annuity is a contract with an insurance company or financial institution that delays payments until a future date chosen by the investor.

q: 61. If valuable properties are found during excavation, it becomes the property of
explain: Per standard contract clauses and the Treasure Trove Act, any fossils, coins, or valuables found during excavation belong to the State/Government.

q: 62. The most reliable estimate is
explain: A detailed estimate is prepared based on actual measurements from drawings and is therefore the most accurate and reliable.

q: 63. Pick up the item of work not included in the plinth area estimate
explain: Plinth area includes the built-up covered area. Courtyards and open spaces are excluded from plinth area calculations.

q: 64. Due to change in price level, a revised estimate is prepared if the sanctioned estimate exceeds
explain: A revised estimate must be prepared if the actual expenditure or the probable cost exceeds the sanctioned amount by more than 5%.

q: 65. The plinth area of a building includes
options: area of walls at floor level
explain: While internal areas like walls and lifts are part of the built-up area, common estimation rules often distinguish what constitutes 'Plinth' vs 'Carpet'. The key indicates cantilevered porches (if covered) are often included.

q: 66. Carpet area does not include the area of
explain: Carpet area is the actual usable area where a carpet can be laid. It excludes walls, balconies, toilets, kitchens, and corridors.

q: 67. The floor area includes the area of the balcony up to
explain: In many building bylaws, only 50% of the balcony area is counted towards the total floor area or Floor Space Index (FSI).

q: 68. The order of booking dimensions is
explain: Standard practice in a measurement book (MB) is to record dimensions in the order: Length (L), Breadth (B), and Height/Depth (H).

q: 69. The brick work is not measured in cu m in case of
options: One or more than one brick wall
explain: Half-brick walls (partition walls) are measured in square metres (m²) because their thickness is a fixed standard (10cm/4.5 inches).

q: 70. The brick work is measured in sq. metre, in case of
options: Half brick walls or the partition
explain: All the listed items have fixed thicknesses and are thus traditionally measured by surface area in m².

q: 71. The measurement is made in square metre in case of
explain: Concrete foundation and RCC work are measured in cubic metres (m³), and hollow block walls are also typically measured in m³ (unless very thin).

q: 72. The measurement is not made in square metres in case of
explain: RCC Chhajjas (projections) are often measured in cubic metres or as a specific item, whereas DPC and formwork are strictly square metre items.

q: 73. The measurement is made for stone work in square metre in case of
explain: Thin stone veneer or wall facing is measured in m², whereas massive stone structures like columns are in m³; however, combined options often point to area-based cladding.

q: 74. The area is measured correct to the nearest
explain: In estimation, all area measurements are recorded to two decimal places, i.e., 0.01 square metres.

q: 75. The volume is measured correct to the nearest
explain: Volume calculations are standardly recorded to two decimal places (0.01 m³).

q: 76. The weight of an item is measured correct to nearest
explain: Structural steel and reinforcement weights are generally rounded to the nearest whole kilogram (1.0 kg).

q: 77. While preparing a detailed estimate
explain: The standard degree of accuracy for dimensions, areas, and volumes in engineering estimates is 0.01 units.

q: 78. The 'center line method' is specially adopted for estimating
explain: The centerline method is the fastest way to estimate quantities for buildings with uniform cross-sections, especially those with circular or polygonal plans.

q: 79. In long and short wall method... length of long wall is the center to center distance plus
options: half breadth of wall on each side
explain: Long wall length = (C/C distance) + (1/2 breadth + 1/2 breadth) = (C/C distance) + Breadth.

q: 80. While estimating a reinforced cement structure, the omitted cover of concrete is assumed
explain: Standard concrete covers (end, side, and bottom) must be subtracted from member dimensions to find the actual length of reinforcement bars.

q: 81. The damp proof course (DPC) is measured in
explain: DPC is a thin layer applied over the plinth; since its thickness is very small and specified, it is measured by area (m²).

q: 82. The rate of an item of work depends on
explain: The unit rate is influenced by the quality of materials (specs), the mix ratio (proportion), and how the work is performed (method).

q: 83. In case of laying gullies, siphons, intercepting traps, the cost includes
explain: When estimating sanitary fixtures, the item rate usually covers the fitting itself, the concrete bed it sits on, and the labor to connect it.

q: 84. Cost of fittings and their fixing is specified for the following sanitary fittings
explain: Items like sinks, WCs, and basins are 'by number' items, and their rate includes the cost of the unit and its installation.

q: 85. The detention period in a septic tank is assumed
explain: While the key indicates 30 minutes (c), in practical engineering, the detention period for a septic tank is actually 24 to 48 hours. (Referencing the provided key).

q: 86. The trap which is provide to disconnect the house drain from the street sewer is called
explain: All these terms refer to the Intercepting Trap located at the last point of the house drainage system before it joins the public sewer.

q: 87. The slope of the outlet of 'P trap' below the horizontal is kept.
explain: The outlet of a P-trap is typically angled slightly downward (approx 14 degrees) to ensure smooth self-cleansing flow.

q: 88. Anti-siphonage pipe is connected to
options: Bottom of P trap W. C.
Top of P trap W. C.
explain: Anti-siphonage pipes are connected to the top of the P-trap to prevent the water seal from being sucked out by atmospheric pressure changes.

q: 89. The height of the sink of wash basin above floor level is kept
explain: Standard ergonomic installation height for a washbasin is between 75 cm and 80 cm from the finished floor level.

q: 90. The cross-sections for a highway is taken at
options: right angle to the center line
explain: Highway cross-sections are surveyed perpendicularly to the alignment at regular intervals (usually 30m) and where the terrain changes significantly.

q: 91. If B is the width of formation, d is the height of embankment, side slope S : 1... the area of cross-section is
explain: Area of a trapezoidal embankment section = Area of central rectangle (B*d) + Area of two side triangles (2 * 1/2 * Sd * d) = Bd + Sd².

q: 92. If the formation level... has a uniform gradient... and the ground is also having a longitudinal slope...
explain: Earthwork volume can be calculated using any of these mathematical methods depending on the required accuracy and ground profile.

q: 93. The correct prismoidal formula for volume is
explain: The Prismoidal rule (Simpson's rule for volume) states V = D/3 [First + Last + 4(Sum of even areas) + 2(Sum of odd areas)].

q: 94. The area of a sloping surface of a protective embankment of mean height d, side slopes S : 1 and length L is
explain: Sloping breadth = √(d² + (Sd)²) = d√(1+S²). Area for one side = L * d√(1+S²).

q: 95. The cross section of a road partly in banking and partly in cutting is
explain: These formulas represent the areas of the cutting and banking portions respectively when a road traverses a side-sloping ground.

q: 96. The area of the cross-section of a road fully in banking, is
explain: This is the general formula for the cross-sectional area of a road on side-sloping ground where 'r' is the ground slope and 's' is the side slope.

q: 97. Berms are provided in canals if these are
options: partly in excavation and partly in embankment
explain: Berms are horizontal ledges left between the top of the cutting and the toe of the bank to improve stability and prevent siltation.

q: 98. The excavation exceeding 1.5 m in width and 10 sq. m in plan area with a depth not exceeding 30 cm, is termed as
explain: Surface excavation refers to wide but shallow digging (up to 30cm depth), distinct from foundation trenching.

q: 99. Pick up the excavation where measurement is made in square meters for payment
options: surface dressing up to 15 cm depths
explain: Shallow works like surface dressing (cleaning) and surface excavation (up to 30cm) are paid by area (m²) rather than volume.

q: 100. Brick walls are measured in sq. m if the thickness of the wall is
explain: Single-layer or half-brick walls (typically 10 cm or 4.5 inches thick) are always measured in square metres.
